# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why1: After I said how supes do the log today, it makes sense to check how that went on the last walk; it is the natural close to the problem step.
screens.why2: Walk, trailer, written up, daily log: these are a super's own words, and every rung reads on the first pass.
screens.why3: Any super knows how long last night's log took and whether it got done that day; it is their own evening.
screens.why4: The rungs cover the range from quick to never done and none is nonsense, but the first measures how soon after the walk the log was typed while the next three measure how long it took, so a super who started late but finished in twenty minutes has no clean answer.
screens.why5: My rungs are kept word for word, but the belief narrows the act to 'typing up the daily log in the trailer', and my pain is the whole end-of-day job, including photo uploads, wherever it gets done; 'the rest of the evening' is often at home.
screens.why7: All five rungs grade time, which is my cost; the first is today's way working and the last is never done; the line under the first leaves one rung against and four for, so the belief can go either way; the escape sits apart.
screens.instead: Think of the last site walk. How long did getting the photos and notes into the daily log take? Done in under half an hour · Took about an hour · Took a couple of hours · Took the rest of the evening · Never got written up that day · Someone else did it

screens.why1: Choosing who asks my superintendents the questions belongs right here, after the problem is set and just before the link goes out by text.
screens.why2: It reads plainly, but it is unclear whether I am picking a face on video or only a voice: the hint says Keel 'records the voice' while the questions are asked 'on video', so I had to read it twice to know what the 400 credits buy.
screens.why3: It is my own launch decision, answerable from knowing my supers, who will mostly open a text in the trailer at the end of the day.
screens.why4: Two named interviewers, each with a 5-second preview and Daphne preselected, is a complete and distinct choice, and the hint covers people who would rather read and tap.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or my buyer roles is restated or changed; the screen only names my respondents as construction superintendents, as I typed them.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions on video? Each one is a face and a voice, and the questions also show as text. Options: Daphne ▶ Hear and see Daphne · 5 s; Saskia ▶ Hear and see Saskia · 5 s. 400 credits, recorded once for this project.

screens.why1: Once I've settled who puts the questions to my supers, the next obvious thing is how they answer, so this fits right before sending.
screens.why2: Each option says plainly what my supers would see and do, and Daphne is explained in the same line, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on their phones in a loud trailer or on site at the end of the day, so I can judge whether talking to a video or tapping fits them.
screens.why4: Video interviewer, read-and-tap, and let-them-choose cover the real choices without overlap, and none is odd.
screens.why5: My pick of Read and tap is kept as I made it, and nothing about Fresco or my roles leaks into what the respondent sees.

screens.why1: Once the interviews are set up, the last thing I need to decide is who gets the link, so this belongs at the end of the flow.
screens.why2: I understand it on first read, but the second option switches from 'I' to 'you send them' halfway through and names a 'Contacts page' I haven't seen in this flow, so I read it twice.
screens.why3: I know who I'd send it to: the supers I've met driving to Napa, South Bay and around SF, each by name.
screens.why4: The three choices are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers (by name, from a search, or one link posted where they gather), and my real answer is the first one.
screens.why5: It keeps my pick of people I know by name, and nothing about Fresco or the contractor buyer shows up here.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? — People I know by name (I send each their own link) / People I find with Keel (I pick a list from a search; Keel makes a link for each and I send them) / A group, with one open link (I post it where supers already are; each signs in with Google)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with the number that decides it, 'Frequency: 4 counted', and the card below adds the missing piece, 5 needed to call it.
screens.why_b2: There's no chart here, but the tally (1 holding, 3 too few to call, 7 answered) and the Prevalence line '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar' tell me what was counted, over how many, and where my bar sits on first look.
screens.why_b3: Three of the four beliefs are about 'searching for a missing site photo', which was a side remark in my launch post; my problem is the hours supers spend in the trailer uploading photos and typing the daily log, and only the Current solution card and the statement up top say that.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do next, such as getting more supers to answer or that the problem is unconfirmed until Frequency, Importance and Current solution can be called; 'What it measures' only explains the method.
screens.why_b5: 'Too few to call' is honest, but 'Holding up' on Prevalence rests on 7 people landing exactly at the bar with no low-n caveat, and the verdict line names only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are just as short.
screens.instead: Not called yet: only 4 of 7 supers could be counted on how often, how much it matters, and how they cope today (5 needed each), so get more superintendents to answer before trusting this. And test my problem, the hours spent in the trailer turning the day's photos and notes into the daily log, not searching for a missing photo.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against over 7 people on a 0-7 axis, with the marker at 6 labelled 'at least 8 in 10', so what is counted, over whom and where my bar sits are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: My problem was the hours of getting the walk's photos and notes into the daily log; 'searched for a missing site photo' is one recognisable piece of that (photos 'aren't very searchable'), but it is narrower than what I counted.
screens.why_b4: 'At your bar exactly' and the pointer to the next two cards are useful, but the card doesn't say what that means for me, for example that one more No would sink it, or what to check before building on it.
screens.why_b5: It keeps to the 7, says 'a small group: a lean, not a call', and calls the result holding, not strong; only the stray '— the most recent time it happened' tag on a yes/no gate is odd, and it doesn't overstate anything.
screens.instead: Holding, but only just: 6 of 7 superintendents searched for a missing site photo this week, exactly your bar of 8 in 10, and one more No would drop it, so treat it as a lean and check the log-writing hours on the next two cards.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right next to the number that decides it, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both together.
screens.why_b2: The axis (working days out of 5) and the median at 5 read at once, but it took me a second look to work out where my bar sits: the legend's 'what you said' vs 'at what you said', the '4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3)' strip, and a 0 tick no superintendent could pick.
screens.why_b3: My problem is the hours spent getting the day's photos and notes into the daily log; 'search for a missing site photo' is a recognisable piece of that, not the act I'd name as the pain.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that all 4 counted sit at or above my low, or that one more counted answer would decide it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, why Hank and Luis are out) and the low n is called 'a lean, not a call', so nothing claims more than the four answers carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 counted searched on 4 or 5 of their last 5 working days, at or above your 4. One more counted answer decides it, so get one more superintendent to answer before you lean on this.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside its number, 4 counted and 5 needed, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 8 picks from 4 people, but the bar is not on the chart, and the strip's "your bar · 4 of 5" with its marker at 4 reads like four of five already for me until I work out it means four of five needed.
screens.why_b3: The people and the moment are mine, though "on commercial jobs" was dropped, but my hurt is the hours of uploading photos and typing up the log after the walks, and "Searching for a missing site photo" is a side complaint from my post rather than the problem I named.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" is a generic line; it doesn't tell me to get more answers, or that the two who left me out both named the schedule and subs over the log.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible and the small group is said, but calling a 2-for, 2-against split "a lean" claims a direction the data doesn't have.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted, split 2 for and 2 against, so no lean either way; the two against both put the schedule and subs ahead of the log. Get at least one more counted answer before reading this.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted with 5 needed, so I know why there's no call yet.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the line under 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' marker next to a 2-in-3 rule and only 4 counted made me stop and work out where 4 of 5 came from.
screens.why_b3: Current solution, typing up the daily log in the trailer, and my own rungs from half an hour through to never written up that day are my words.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't say that 3 of the 4 counted fell short or that one more counted super would settle it.
screens.why_b5: n is visible, the two uncounted people are named with reasons, and the small group is called a lean, not a call, with no claim beyond it.
screens.instead: 3 of 4 counted supers took an hour or more after the walk, a lean your way; one more counted answer decides it, so get one more super through, and label the strip marker 'needs 4 of 5' rather than 'your bar · 4 of 5'.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Importance is my dimension, but the belief reads 'searching for a missing site photo', when what I checked was the hours of turning the day's photos and notes into the daily log; the quotes then talk about the log, not photo search, so the line is recognisable but off from mine.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what this means for Fresco; it doesn't say to get one more superintendent's answer, and it doesn't say that schedule and subs outranking the log is a positioning problem for a log tool.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked here), the low count is named as too few, and no claim reaches past the two people quoted.
screens.why_b6: The group name just rejoins two of my own Importance options (schedule, subs), though Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise finishing on the tablet before the gate do hint that the log is deferrable for some supers.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 counted. The two who ranked other things higher picked the schedule and no-show subs, and one said the log can wait till morning. Get one more superintendent's answer, and ask whether Fresco can feed the schedule and the sub follow-ups and not only the log.

screens.why1: As the first screen, it makes sense to check that my jobs run on Procore or ACC before asking me anything about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms my jobs actually run on, so I know them at a glance, though saying 'run' twice is a little clunky.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my jobs is on, so I can answer this right away.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers every case, since a job on Procore, on ACC, or on both is a Yes, and anything else is a No, and a gate question needs no escape.
screens.why5: It names the platforms the study is screening for and gives away nothing about any product or what the founder plans to build.
screens.why6: Short and spoken as one question with a plain yes or no, and A-C-C said as letters is how we say it on site anyway.
screens.instead: Are any of the jobs you're running now on Procore or ACC? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after confirming I'm on Procore or ACC, asking whether I had to hunt for a photo this week is the obvious next step before they ask for the story.
screens.why2: Searching for a missing site photo is something I've done, digging through my phone roll or Procore for the shot of the slab before the pour, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know whether I went looking for a photo I couldn't find in the last week; no guessing needed.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the chips only belong to the story box after a Yes.
screens.why5: It asks about the part that hurts, the photo I couldn't find, without naming any product or the company's plan, so nothing leaks to me.
screens.why6: It's one short question with 'Yes or no' at the end, easy to answer by ear.
screens.why7: Two fixed answers in order and no escape at the gate; a super whose photos were all where they should be truly says No, and one who went digging says Yes, so the founder's share can be supported or refuted.

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to hunting for a missing photo this week, it's obvious to ask how many days that happened.
screens.why2: I'd read it twice over 'missing': does it mean a shot I took and can't find in my camera roll or Procore, or one that never got taken, and does scrolling for the right shot every afternoon count?
screens.why3: I know roughly which days this week I was digging through my phone or the Procore photos for a shot, so I can count it.
screens.why4: One through five covers the week, each is distinct, nobody past a yes needs a zero, and 'I can't recall' fits apart.
screens.why5: Nothing about anyone's product or plan comes through, just a plain question about my week.
screens.why6: One short question with 'a number from 1 to 5' and one escape, easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Every option counts working days in the window from 1 to 5, the unit is said once, the act is one thing that happened on a day or didn't, and the lone escape is there; balance depends on the founder's low, which isn't shown here.
screens.instead: On how many of the last 5 working days did you hunt for a site photo you'd taken but couldn't find? 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 · I can't recall

screens.why1: Right after asking how often I hunted for a missing photo, it makes sense to ask how that stacks up against the other stuff I'm stuck doing after the walk.
screens.why2: Subs, schedule, safety items, RFIs and site photos are all words I use every day, though "your last day of site walks" is a little odd since I walk every day.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I personally deal with once the walks are done, so I can answer without guessing.
screens.why4: The options are distinct and in my words, but what actually eats my evening, getting the photos and notes uploaded and typed into the daily log, isn't on the list, so I'd pick the photo search or the schedule by default.
screens.why5: Nothing here tells me about a product or an AI scribe, and the photo-search row matches what I was just asked about.
screens.why6: Five short options, read as a list with one escape at the end; the RFI one is the longest but still easy to hold.
screens.why7: The own row is on the list, not first, with three or more rivals and None of these at the first ask, so it can go either way, but the rivals are other after-walk chores rather than troubles in getting the day into the log, which bends the rule that rivals stay in the moment the circumstance names.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Searching for a missing site photo · Sorting the day's photos into the log · Typing up the day's notes into the log · Tagging photos to the right location · None of these

screens.why1: After asking which part of the site-walk day I'd want easier, asking how my last daily log write-up went is the obvious next question, and this time the stem and the options are both about the log.
screens.why2: Daily log, the trailer, the walk: that's how I talk about my day, and I get it on one read.
screens.why3: I know exactly how long my last log took and when it got done, so I don't have to guess.
screens.why4: The bands leave gaps: 45 minutes or an hour and a half doesn't clearly land anywhere, and the anchors shift between 'of the walk', 'in the trailer' and 'after the walk', so a log I knocked out at home in an hour has no clean fit.
screens.why5: It reads as a straight question about my log time with nothing about anybody's product or their own labels for me.
screens.why6: Short stem, five short parallel time phrases and one escape at the end, so I can hold it when it's read to me and answer.
screens.why7: Every rung is on one measure, time spent writing the log, with a working rung first and an outright failure last, and the escape is there, but the bands don't meet each other, so some true answers are left out.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did writing it up take? Under half an hour; half an hour to an hour; one to two hours; more than two hours; never got done that day. Or say someone else did it.
